Record Q2 net new ARR of $221 million, over 1,000 Flex customers, and more than 100 re-flexes highlight CrowdStrike as the leader in cybersecurity consolidation.” CrowdStrike CEO, on the earnings call · For Q3 FY26, CrowdStrike guided total revenue of $1,208.0 to $1,218.0 million, non-GAAP income from operations of $256.0 to $262.0 million, non-GAAP net income attributable to CrowdStrike of $238.1 to $242.8 million, and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.93 to $0.95 on 257 million weighted average diluted shares.
The cybersecurity firm posted non-GAAP EPS of $0.93, ahead of the $0.83 consensus estimate by 12.05%, while revenue grew 21.3% year over year to $1.17 billion, edging past the $1.15 billion consensus by 1.63%. The headline driver was a reacceleration in net new Annual Recurring Revenue, which reached $221.10 million for the quarter, arriving ahead of management's own timeline as deepening module adoption, with 48% of customers on six or more modules, continued to fuel expansion within the existing base. Total ARR climbed 20% year over year to $4.66 billion. Looking ahead, CrowdStrike guided Q3 revenue to $1.21 billion to $1.22 billion and raised its full-year FY26 revenue outlook to $4.75 billion to $4.81 billion, with non-GAAP EPS expected in the range of $3.60 to $3.72.
For full year FY26, guidance was raised to total revenue of $4,749.5 to $4,805.5 million, non-GAAP income from operations of $1,000.1 to $1,040.1 million, non-GAAP net income of $922.4 to $954.0 million, and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $3.60 to $3.72 on 256 million weighted average diluted shares. Both periods assume a 21.0% non-GAAP tax rate. Management expressed conviction in continued net new ARR acceleration for the back half of FY26.
CrowdStrike delivered a solid beat on both the top and bottom lines in its second quarter of fiscal 2026, though shares fell sharply after results as investors focused on a Q3 revenue outlook that landed below some expectations.
